marble.name: Earth's Layers
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Know that Earth has layers — a thin outer crust, a thick hot mantle, and a core at the centre — and that the inside of the Earth is extremely hot
marble.prompt: If you cracks open a hard-boiled egg, can they compare it to Earth and name the three layers — crust on the outside, mantle in the middle, and core at the centre?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning about powerful forces that shape our Earth — understanding what volcanoes and earthquakes are, how they change the landscape, and important safety rules to follow during earthquakes.

misconceptions: The crust is thick / a large fraction of the Earth (it is a very thin skin by comparison).
The whole inside of the Earth is liquid lava/molten rock (much of the interior is solid or very stiff rock; the outer core is liquid metal, the inner core solid).
The centre is hollow, or filled with air/water, or that people/creatures could live inside.
'Lava' fills the Earth (magma forms only in specific hot regions; the term 'lava' applies only at the surface).
The layers are cold like ordinary underground soil (the interior is extremely hot, increasing with depth).
representations: Labelled cutaway sphere of Earth (crust, mantle, core) — the canonical diagram
Apple / hard-boiled-egg / peach analogy for the thin crust relative to the whole
A temperature gradient bar or colour ramp that heats up as you go deeper toward the core
A 'drill probe' descending inward, passing named layers, as a way to feel scale and depth
authoredAnswer: We stand on the crust, the outermost layer. It's extremely THIN compared with the layers below — like the skin on an apple compared with the whole apple. Beneath it is the thick, very hot mantle, and at the centre the core. The inside of the Earth is hot enough to melt rock.

wrongAnswers.wrong: The crust is a thick layer, about the same as the others.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Draws or describes the crust roughly as thick as the mantle.
wrongAnswers.fix: Show a to-scale slice — the crust is a hair-thin skin on a huge hot interior.

wrongAnswers.wrong: The inside of the Earth is cool or only a bit warm.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Denies the interior is hot enough to melt rock.
wrongAnswers.fix: Link to volcanoes and geothermal heat — the interior is thousands of degrees.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Says everything under the crust is liquid.
wrongAnswers.fix: The mantle is mostly solid hot rock (soft, slow-flowing); only the outer core is truly liquid.
